svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "The polymerase chain reaction (PCR) makes millions of copies of a DNA sequence."], [1, "Denaturation at about 95 \u00b0C: the strands separate."], [3.5, "Annealing at about 60 \u00b0C: primers bind to the ends of the target."], [6, "Extension at 72 \u00b0C: Taq polymerase builds new strands from the primers."], [9, "One cycle has doubled the DNA. Repeating the cycle doubles it again each time."], [13, "2\u207f: after 30 cycles there are more than a billion copies."]]
svg.title: PCR
svg.desc: One cycle of the polymerase chain reaction: denaturation at 95 C separates strands, primers anneal at about 60 C, Taq polymerase extends them at 72 C; the temperature graph and exponential doubling of copies.
svg.text: Target region shown in colour; primers in orange.

g.data-info: Heat breaks the hydrogen bonds between bases, separating the two DNA strands.
Cooling lets short primers bind (by complementary base pairing) to each strand at either end of the target sequence.
Taq DNA polymerase, an enzyme from a thermophilic bacterium that is not denatured at 95 °C, adds free nucleotides from each primer, copying the strand 5′ → 3′.
A machine that changes the temperature automatically for each stage.
Each cycle doubles the number of copies of the target: after n cycles, 2ⁿ copies. 30 cycles: over a billion copies in a few hours.
g.text: Copies of the target after each cycle
